title: SLO-led compensation allocator with KV soft-shedding
creator: Ava Gardner
description:
Problem: As continuous batching scales, tight GPU memory and KV cache pressure cause tail latency spikes when large requests or hot KV working sets arrive. Current preemption policies are blunt (hard kill or blind lease reclaim) and hurt both SLO-sensitive tenants and overall throughput. We need a scheduler that: 1) enforces tenant SLOs (p99/p95 latency targets, burst budgets), 2) performs soft, compensating actions (temporary batching holdbacks, degraded but bounded KV eviction, adaptive timebox leases) rather than hard termination, and 3) balances long-term fairness so noisy tenants can’t starve others.

Proposal summary: Implement a SLO-led Compensation Allocator (SCA) that monitors per-tenant latency envelopes and GPU/KV residency signals and applies graded mitigation actions. Mitigations are ordered by impact and reversibility: (A) micro-holdback of new requests into a short timebox, (B) switch to lighter-weight model quantization variant for the affected slices, (C) soft KV-shedding (evict cold prefixes and shadow evict candidates to coldstore), (D) short-lived lease shrink (reduce KV lease size for excess tenants), (E) hard preempt as last resort. The allocator uses a compensation budget per tenant derived from recent SLO compliance and credit accounting. The system prefers actions that preserve correctness and model outputs while relieving memory pressure.

Design notes: - Signals used: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, token rate, KV-residency fraction (hotset percentage), GPU memory headroom, batch queue depth, ongoing model quantization compatibility flags. - Policy engine: rule-graph where each rule has triggers (thresholds, trend windows), mitigation sequences, and cost estimates (expected latency delta, memory reclaimed). - Lease accounting: implement a soft lease token that encodes nominal KV bytes and a volatility score; leases can be shrunk temporarily with grace-window callbacks to callers. - Fairness: proportional-credit rebalancer where tenants earn credit for staying within SLOs; credits permit temporary extra residency; credits decay over time. - Configuration: runtime knobs exposed via Console and API: global memory-safety margin, per-tenant SLO profile, mitigation ordering overrides, recovery window durations.

Why different from existing approaches: Instead of only enforcing hard preemption or equal-time-slicing, SCA uses compensating steps that are reversible and minimize correctness regression. It couples tenant-level SLO accounting with memory-aware eviction hints so KV eviction is targeted (cold prefixes and low-reuse keys), avoiding wholesale cache flushes.
acceptance_criteria: SCA deployed behind feature flag on a dedicated cluster
Demonstrated reduction in p99 tail spikes under synthetic KV-hot workload by >=30% without >5% throughput loss
No customer-visible incorrect outputs from mitigation steps (quantization fallback, lease shrink) beyond defined tolerances
Telemetry: new per-tenant compensation budget metrics are emitted and dashboarded
Automated e2e tests for each mitigation step and rollback path
metrics: KV residency delta per-tenant (bytes) after soft-shedding
frequency and duration of timebox holdbacks
rollout_plan: 1) Implement policy engine and local simulator; unit tests for rule graph. 2) Canary deploy SCA in feature-flagged mode on non-prod cluster with synthetic KV-hot scenarios. 3) Enable soft-shedding and timebox holdbacks only (no hard preempt) for 2 small production shards; monitor metrics for 72 hours. 4) Gradually enable lease shrink and quantization fallback for additional shards if metrics meet success criteria. 5) After 2 weeks stable, enable full mitigation ordering including hard preempt as last-resort. Console flags: "fast_revert" to immediately reverse mitigations. Rollback: disable feature flag and allow leases to recover over window.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Initial draft: scoped mitigation list and signals. Requested review from infra and runtime teams (Marcus, Priya).
2025-02-25 - Marcus: added proportional-credit model and suggested per-tenant hysteresis to prevent oscillation. Updated mitigation ordering to prefer timebox before KV eviction.

2025-03-03 - Performance: ran simulator with 10k-tenants synthetic trace; soft-shedding prevented 78% of hard preempt cases in the trace. Need unit tests for lease shrink callbacks and a canary dashboard panel for compensation budget burn rate.
2025-03-05 - Security: SLO actions do not expose PII. Confirmed KMS/HSM interactions not required for this change. Marked security_review_required=false.
blockers: Need deterministic simulator seed for reproducible tests (blocking PR: runtime/simulator#512). Also require small API change to KV service to accept "soft-evict" hints with callback token (engineering review pending).
